{"function": "write_file", "params": {"path": "solution.py", "content": "import sys
v=list(map(int,sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()));n,k=v[:2];k=min(n,k);p=2;costs=[]
for i in range(n):costs.append(v[p:p+n-i]);p+=n-i
columns=n+k;INF=10**100;cost=[[INF]*(columns+1) for _ in range(n+1)]
for job in range(1,n+1):
 for slot in range(1,k+1):cost[job][slot]=costs[0][job-1]
 for previous in range(1,job):cost[job][k+previous]=costs[previous][job-previous-1]
u=[0]*(n+1);pot=[0]*(columns+1);matching=[0]*(columns+1);way=[0]*(columns+1)
for row in range(1,n+1):
 matching[0]=row;j0=0;minimum=[INF]*(columns+1);used=[False]*(columns+1)
 while True:
  used[j0]=True;i0=matching[j0];delta=INF;j1=0
  for j in range(1,columns+1):
   if not used[j]:
    value=cost[i0][j]-u[i0]-pot[j]
    if value<minimum[j]:minimum[j]=value;way[j]=j0
    if minimum[j]<delta:delta=minimum[j];j1=j
  for j in range(columns+1):
   if used[j]:u[matching[j]]+=delta;pot[j]-=delta
   else:minimum[j]-=delta
  j0=j1
  if matching[j0]==0:break
 while j0:previous=way[j0];matching[j0]=matching[previous];j0=previous
print(sum(cost[matching[j]][j] for j in range(1,columns+1) if matching[j]))
"}}
```

stdio_review.algorithm_assessment: Assign each request one predecessor: either one of k interchangeable company-start slots or an earlier request. Each predecessor slot is used at most once. Since request edges only go forward in time, every complete assignment forms disjoint chronological team routes, with at most k starts and all requests covered. Rectangular minimum-cost assignment therefore minimizes all actual equipment moves without forcing every team to be used or charging return trips. Use raw asymmetric move costs rather than assuming triangle inequalities.
stdio_review.limitations: One source reviewer plus actual isolated tests, not independent dual semantic review.

stdio_review.algorithm_assessment: After a new order arrives, any later meal previously assigned to an older order can move to this newer order without increasing its price or violating shelf life. Thus orders partition days into consecutive blocks. A block of d days costs the fee plus the sum of the cheapest prices with shelf life at least0..d-1; these marginal prices are nondecreasing, giving a convex block-cost function. For fixed delivery count, balanced block lengths minimize total cost. Its perspective as a function of delivery count is convex, so discrete slope binary search finds the global minimum, including the maximum-shelf-life lower bound. A second monotone search finds the maximum affordable days with exact integer arithmetic.
